A.notes: All checks pass; solid rule tests (35) incl. castling-through-check and ep pin. Bug: defender reply setTimeout (A/diff.patch:542) is never cancelled, and startPuzzle (A/diff.patch:461) does not clear it, so switching puzzle within 450 ms plays the old reply and bumps step on the new puzzle. Clean but plain UI with a sparse desktop sidebar.

B.notes: No real bugs found. Accepts any move that still forces mate (B/diff.patch:1112), cancels the reply timer (B/diff.patch:1060), uses pointer capture, and has a real touch-drag e2e test. Very polished UI: move list, puzzle grid with solved ticks, modal results with View board. main.ts at 673 lines is large but readable.

C.notes: No real bugs found. The defender reply is applied synchronously and animated (C/diff.patch:1010), so there is no timer race. Broadest tests: 53 unit (extra perft positions, puzzle validation) and 15 e2e incl. touch tap/drag, castling and threefold via the UI. Most polished UI: overlays, move list, puzzle grid, hint. CSS is heavy (648 lines).

D.notes: Rules are correct and well tested (43). Bug: the reply setTimeout (D/diff.patch:655) is not tracked or cleared by resetTransient (D/diff.patch:587), so changing puzzle during the 450 ms delay plays the old reply on the new puzzle. UI is decent with a puzzle grid, but the promotion picker has no label and New game is duplicated in the mate state.

E.notes: Engine is fine (21 tests, fewest). Bug: the async reply (E/diff.patch:624) cannot be cancelled, giving the same race on puzzle change. The UI is minimal: only New game (no flip or undo), a small centred board with a mostly empty 1280 px layout, and odd king glyphs, so item 11 polish is only partly met.

F.notes: Bug: the reply setTimeout (F/diff.patch:567) is never cleared on puzzle change. Checking an alternative mate replays the whole line from the puzzle FEN (F/diff.patch:538) instead of using the current game. The phone header layout differs between modes, Puzzle solved shows three times, the knight and king glyphs look rough, and puzzles are chosen from a dropdown.

G.notes: No real bugs found. A cleanly modular engine (board/movegen/game) and UI, with 65 unit tests incl. SAN disambiguation. The reply timer is cleared (G/diff.patch:1329) and wrong moves are undone with a SAN message. Polished green board, move list, puzzle grid and checkmate overlay. Touch drag was only checked manually via CDP, not in e2e.

X.notes: No real bugs found. Modular engine with colocated tests (69 unit, incl. per-puzzle solution validation). Timers are tracked and cleared (X/diff.patch:1707). Only 4 e2e tests, and touch drag is untested (its own report admits this). Polished branded UI with an amber accent, move list, puzzle grid and game-over modal. A wrong move is shown, then taken back after 700 ms.

Y.notes: No real bugs found. Timers are tracked and cleared (Y/diff.patch:540), and alternative mates are accepted via a probe game. Tests are adequate (42). The UI is plain: duplicate solved cards (Puzzle solved plus Solved!), a Game over card that holds only Flip board, and no move list.

Z.notes: No real bugs found. The reply timer is cleared on navigation (Z/diff.patch:529). The e2e test solves all 12 puzzles and covers castling and en passant via the UI. A wrong move is flagged by a message only, with no square highlight (Z/diff.patch:590). Clean, consistent UI in both themes with a solid promotion dialog, but the desktop layout is sparse and there is no move list.
